title.zh: 卷一百四十 列傳第九十: 韋皋 張建封 盧群
title.en: Volume 140 Biographies 90: Wei Gao, Zhang Jianfeng, Lu Qun
title.raw: 卷一百四十 列傳第九十: 韋皋 張建封 盧群 Volume 140 Biographies 90: Wei Gao, Zhang Jianfeng, Lu Qun

sentences.zh: 韋臯，字城武，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Gao, courtesy name Chengwu, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, whose courtesy name was Chengwu, came from the capital district of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，以建陵挽郎調補華州參軍，累授使府監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, he was transferred from a Jianling pallbearer post to fill a Huazhou staff assistant position, and was repeatedly appointed supervisory censor in military commissioners' offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali reign he left a Jianling pallbearer appointment for a staff post in Huazhou, and over time rose to serve as supervisory censor under successive military governors.

sentences.zh: 宰相張鎰出為鳳翊隴右節度使，奏臯為營田判官，得殿中侍御史，權知隴州行營留後事。

translations.literal: When the chief minister Zhang Yin went out as military governor of Fengyi and Longyou, he memorialized to appoint Gao as agricultural colony judge, obtained the post of palace supervisory censor, and had him act as temporary Longzhou campaign rear administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After Chief Minister Zhang Yin took up the Fengyi–Longyou command, he had Gao named agricultural colony judge, secured him a palace censor's title, and entrusted him with acting authority over Longzhou's campaign rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，涇師犯闕，德宗幸奉天，鳳翔兵馬使李楚琳殺張鎰，以府城叛歸於硃泚，隴州刺史郝通奔於楚琳。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, the Jingzhou troops stormed the capital, Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Fengxiang military envoy Li Chulin killed Zhang Yin and surrendered the prefectural city to Zhu Ci, and Longzhou prefect Hao Tong fled to Chulin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4 the Jingzhou mutineers attacked the capital, forcing Emperor Dezong to take refuge at Fengtian; Fengxiang's military envoy Li Chulin murdered Zhang Yin, handed the city to Zhu Ci, and Longzhou prefect Hao Tong threw in his lot with Chulin.

sentences.zh: 先是，硃泚自范陽入朝，以甲士自隨；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhu Ci had come to court from Fanyang, he had brought armored soldiers with him;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Ci had come to court from Fanyang, he had brought his own armored escort;

sentences.zh: 後泚為鳳翔節度使，既罷，留范陽五百人戍隴州，而泚舊將牛雲光督之。

translations.literal: Later, when Ci became Fengxiang military governor and then left that post, he left five hundred Fanyang men to garrison Longzhou under his former general Niu Yunguang.
translations.idiomatic: After he served as Fengxiang military governor and left office, he left five hundred Fanyang troops to garrison Longzhou under his former officer Niu Yunguang.

sentences.zh: 時泚既以逆徒圍奉天，雲光因稱疾，請臯為帥，將謀亂，擒臯以赴泚。

translations.literal: At that time Ci was already besieging Fengtian with rebels; Yunguang feigned illness, asked Gao to take command, plotted rebellion, and intended to seize Gao and deliver him to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: With Ci's rebels already besieging Fengtian, Yunguang pretended to be ill, asked Gao to assume command, and plotted to seize him and hand him over to Ci.

sentences.zh: 臯將翟曄伺知之，白臯為備；

translations.literal: Gao's officer Zhai Ye learned of it through surveillance and informed Gao to take precautions;
translations.idiomatic: Gao's officer Zhai Ye discovered the plot and warned him to prepare;

sentences.zh: 雲光知事泄，遂率其兵以奔泚。

translations.literal: When Yunguang learned the affair had leaked, he led his troops and fled to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yunguang learned the plot had been exposed, he marched his troops off to join Ci.

sentences.zh: 行及汧陽，遇泚家僮蘇玉將使於臯所，蘇玉謂雲光曰：「太尉已登寶位，使我持詔以韋臯為御史中丞，君可以兵歸隴州。

translations.literal: When they reached Qianyang, they met Ci's household slave Su Yu, who was being sent on a mission to Gao's post; Su Yu said to Yunguang, "The Grand Preceptor has already ascended the throne and sent me with an edict appointing Wei Gao as vice censor-in-chief; you may return your troops to Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the road at Qianyang they met Ci's household slave Su Yu, bound for Gao's headquarters. Su Yu told Yunguang, "The Grand Preceptor has already taken the throne and sent me with an edict naming Wei Gao vice censor-in-chief; you can bring your troops back to Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 臯若承命，即為吾人；

translations.literal: If Gao accepts the command, he will be one of us;
translations.idiomatic: If Gao accepts the edict, he will be on our side;

sentences.zh: 如不受詔，彼書生，可以圖之，事無不濟矣。」

translations.literal: if he does not receive the edict, he is only a scholar—you can deal with him, and nothing will fail."
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses the edict, he is only a scholar—you can take him, and the matter is as good as done."

sentences.zh: 乃反昪疾趨隴州。

translations.literal: Thereupon they turned back and, feigning illness, hurried to Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They turned back at once and, still feigning illness, pressed on to Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 臯迎勞之，先納蘇玉，受其偽命，乃問雲光曰：「始不告而去，今又來，何也？」

translations.literal: Gao went out to welcome and console them, first received Su Yu, accepted the false appointment, and then asked Yunguang, "At first you left without telling me; now you have come again—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao went out to receive them cordially, took Su Yu in first, accepted the bogus appointment, and then asked Yunguang, "You slipped away without a word before—what brings you back now?"

sentences.zh: 雲光曰：「前未知公心，故潛去；

translations.literal: Yunguang said, "Before I did not know your mind, so I left secretly;
translations.idiomatic: Yunguang replied, "I left in secret because I did not yet know where you stood;

sentences.zh: 知公有新命，今乃復還。

translations.literal: now that I know you have a new appointment, I have returned.
translations.idiomatic: now that I know you have received a new commission, I have come back.

sentences.zh: 願與公戮力定功，同其生死。」

translations.literal: I wish to join my strength with yours to establish merit and share life and death."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to join forces with you, share the glory, and stand or fall together."

sentences.zh: 臯曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Gao said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 又謂雲光曰：「大使茍不懷詐，請納器甲，使城中無所危疑，乃可入。」

translations.literal: He also said to Yunguang, "If the envoy truly harbors no deceit, please hand over weapons and armor so that the city may be free of alarm and suspicion; only then may you enter."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If you mean no treachery, surrender your arms and armor first so the city will have no cause for fear—only then may your men enter."

sentences.zh: 雲光以書生待臯，且以為信然，乃盡付弓矢戈甲。

translations.literal: Yunguang treated Gao as a mere scholar and moreover believed it true, so he handed over all bows, arrows, spears, and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Taking Gao for a mere scholar and believing Su Yu's story, Yunguang turned over every bow, arrow, spear, and suit of armor.

sentences.zh: 臯既受之，乃內其兵。

translations.literal: Once Gao had received them, he admitted their troops inside.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao had the weapons, he let the troops into the city.

sentences.zh: 明日，臯犒宴蘇玉、雲光之卒於郡舍，伏甲於兩廊。

translations.literal: The next day Gao feasted Su Yu's and Yunguang's soldiers at the prefectural residence, with armored men hidden in both corridors.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he entertained Su Yu's and Yunguang's men at the prefectural hall, with armed men concealed in both side corridors.

sentences.zh: 酒既行，伏發，盡誅之，斬雲光、蘇玉首以徇。

translations.literal: When the wine had been served, the ambush sprang forth and all were executed; the heads of Yunguang and Su Yu were cut off and displayed.
translations.idiomatic: As the banquet began, the hidden troops rushed out and slaughtered them all; Gao had Yunguang's and Su Yu's heads cut off and displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 泚又使家僮劉海廣以臯為鳳翔節度使，臯斬海廣及從者三人，生一人，使報泚。

translations.literal: Ci again sent his household slave Liu Haiguang to appoint Gao Fengxiang military governor; Gao beheaded Haiguang and three attendants, spared one alive, and sent him to report to Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Ci sent another household slave, Liu Haiguang, to name Gao Fengxiang military governor; Gao executed Haiguang and three of his escorts, spared one man, and sent him back to Ci with the news.

sentences.zh: 於是詔以臯為御史大夫、隴州刺史，置奉義軍節度以旌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Gao censor-in-chief and Longzhou prefect and established the Fengyi Army command to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then appointed Gao censor-in-chief and Longzhou prefect and created the Fengyi Army command to honor his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 臯遣從兄平及弇繼入奉天城，城中聞臯有備，士氣增倍。

translations.literal: Gao sent his cousin Ping and Yan Ji into Fengtian; when the city heard that Gao was prepared, morale doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent his cousin Ping and Yan Ji into beleaguered Fengtian, and when the garrison learned he had secured Longzhou, their spirits soared.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，拜檢校戶部尚書，兼成都尹、御史大夫、劍南西川節度使，代張延賞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was appointed acting minister of revenue, concurrently Chengdu magistrate, censor-in-chief, and Jiannan West Circuit military governor, replacing Zhang Yanshang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 he was made acting minister of revenue, concurrently magistrate of Chengdu, censor-in-chief, and military governor of Jiannan West, succeeding Zhang Yanshang.

sentences.zh: 臯以雲南蠻眾數十萬，與吐蕃和好，蕃人入寇，必以蠻為前鋒。

translations.literal: Gao considered that the Yunnan barbarians numbered several hundred thousand, were on good terms with Tibet, and whenever Tibetans invaded they always used the barbarians as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao saw that the Yunnan tribes numbered in the hundreds of thousands, were allied with Tibet, and invariably served as the vanguard whenever Tibetan armies raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年，臯遣判官崔佐時入南詔蠻，說令向化，以離吐蕃之助。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he sent judge Cui Zuoshi into the Nanzhao barbarians to persuade them to turn toward civilization and thereby sever Tibetan support.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent his judge Cui Zuoshi into Nanzhao to win them over and break their alliance with Tibet.

sentences.zh: 佐時至蠻國羊咀咩城，其王異牟尋忻然接遇，請絕吐蕃，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: When Zuoshi reached the barbarian capital Yangjumie, King Yimouxun received him gladly, asked to break with Tibet, and sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the Nanzhao capital of Yangjumie, King Yimouxun welcomed Cui Zuoshi warmly, agreed to break with Tibet, and sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其年，遣東蠻鬼主驃傍、苴夢沖、苴烏等相率入朝。

translations.literal: That year the Eastern Barbarian spirit-lords Piao Pang, Ju Mengchong, Ju Wu, and others led one another to court.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Eastern Barbarian chieftains Piao Pang, Ju Mengchong, Ju Wu, and others came to court in a body.

sentences.zh: 南蠻自巂州陷沒，臣屬吐蕃，絕朝貢者二十余年，至是復通。

translations.literal: The southern barbarians, since the fall of Xi Prefecture, had submitted to Tibet and had broken off tribute for more than twenty years; now contact was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The southern tribes had not sent tribute for more than twenty years, not since Xi Prefecture fell and they became Tibetan subjects; now the connection was renewed.

sentences.zh: 五年，臯遣大將王有道簡習精卒以入蕃界，與東蠻於故巂州臺登北谷大破吐蕃青海、臘城二節度，斬首二千級，生擒籠官四十五人，其投崖谷而死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Gao sent the great general Wang Youdao to select and drill elite troops to enter Tibetan territory; together with the Eastern Barbarians at the north valley of Taideng in old Xi Prefecture they routed the Tibetan Qinghai and Lachang commands, beheaded two thousand, captured forty-five junior officers alive, and those who plunged from cliffs and ravines to their deaths were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Gao sent General Wang Youdao with picked troops into Tibetan territory; allied with the Eastern Barbarians he smashed the Qinghai and Lachang commands at Taideng north of old Xi Prefecture, taking two thousand heads, forty-five officers alive, and countless more who died fleeing over cliffs.

sentences.zh: 蕃將乞臧遮遮者，蕃之驍將也，久為邊患。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Qizang Zhezhe was Tibet's fierce warrior and had long been a frontier scourge.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan commander Qizang Zhezhe was among their fiercest fighters and had long terrorized the border.

sentences.zh: 自擒遮遮，城柵無不降，數年之內，終復巂州，以功加吏部尚書。

translations.literal: From the capture of Zhezhe, fortresses and stockades surrendered without exception; within several years Xi Prefecture was finally recovered, and for this merit he was promoted to minister of civil appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhezhe's capture, one Tibetan strongpoint after another surrendered, and within a few years Gao recovered Xi Prefecture and was promoted to minister of civil appointments for his service.

sentences.zh: 九年，朝廷築鹽州城，慮為吐蕃掩襲，詔臯出兵牽維之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the court was building Salt Prefecture and, fearing a Tibetan surprise attack, ordered Gao to send troops to tie them down.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, as the court fortified Salt Prefecture and feared a Tibetan strike, Gao was ordered to launch a diversionary campaign.

sentences.zh: 乃命大將董勔、張芬出西山及南道，破峨和城、通鶴軍。

translations.literal: He then ordered the great generals Dong Kan and Zhang Fen to advance by the western mountains and the southern route, capturing Ehe City and Tonghe Army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Generals Dong Kan and Zhang Fen along the western mountains and the southern route, taking Ehe City and the Tonghe garrison.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃南道元帥論莽熱率眾來援，又破之，殺傷數千人，焚定廉城。

translations.literal: The Tibetan southern-route commander Lun Mangre led troops to the rescue; they were defeated again, with several thousand killed or wounded, and Dinglian City was burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan southern commander Lun Mangre marched to relieve them but was beaten again; thousands were killed or wounded and Dinglian City was burned.

sentences.zh: 凡平堡柵五十余所，以功進位檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In all more than fifty forts and stockades were taken, and for this merit he was advanced to acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In all they reduced more than fifty forts and stockades, and Gao was promoted to acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臯又招撫西山羌女、訶陵、白狗、逋租、弱水、南王等八國酋長，入貢闕廷。

translations.literal: Gao also won over the chieftains of the eight western mountain states—Qiangnu, Heling, Baitou, Bozu, Ruoshui, Nanwang, and others—to come to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gao also brought in the chieftains of eight western mountain peoples—among them Qiangnu, Heling, Baitou, Bozu, Ruoshui, and Nanwang—to present tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，加統押近界諸蠻、西山八國兼雲南安撫等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he was additionally made commissioner for overseeing nearby barbarians, the eight western mountain states, and Yunnan pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year he was also named commissioner to oversee the nearby tribes, the eight western mountain states, and Yunnan pacification.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，就加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year he was further appointed associate director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year he was made associate director of the Imperial Secretariat on the spot.

sentences.zh: 十三年，收復巂州城。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the city of Xi Prefecture was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he recovered the city of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，臯命將出軍，累破吐蕃於黎、巂二州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Gao ordered generals to take the field and repeatedly defeated Tibet at Li and Xi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he sent his generals out and won repeated victories over Tibet in Li and Xi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃怒，遂大搜閱，築壘造舟，欲謀入寇，臯悉挫之。

translations.literal: Tibet grew angry, then conducted a great levy, built ramparts and constructed boats, and planned an invasion; Gao thwarted it all.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tibet mobilized on a large scale, built fortifications and boats, and prepared a major invasion, but Gao frustrated every move.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃酋帥兼監統曩貢、臘城等九節度嬰、籠官馬定德與其大將八十七人舉部落來降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Tibetan chieftain and overseer of the nine commands Nanggong, Lachang, and others—Ying, junior officer Ma Dingde, and eighty-seven of his great generals—brought their tribes to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Tibetan overseer of nine commands, junior officer Ma Dingde, and eighty-seven senior commanders brought their tribes over to the Tang side.

sentences.zh: 定德有計略，習知兵法及山川地形，吐蕃每用兵，定德常乘驛計事，蕃中諸將稟其成算。

translations.literal: Dingde had stratagems, was versed in military arts and mountain-and-river terrain; whenever Tibet used troops, Dingde often rode post-horses to plan affairs, and the Tibetan generals followed his completed calculations.
translations.idiomatic: Dingde was a strategist who knew warfare and the mountain terrain intimately; whenever Tibet campaigned he galloped along the courier routes to lay plans, and Tibetan generals fought by his designs.

sentences.zh: 至是，自以扞邊失律，懼得罪而歸心焉。

translations.literal: At this point, believing he had failed in defending the border and fearing punishment, he turned his heart to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Now, fearing punishment for his failures on the frontier, he chose to defect.

sentences.zh: 十七年，吐蕃昆明城管些蠻千余戶又降。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year more than a thousand households of the Guanxie barbarians under Tibetan Kunming City also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year more than a thousand households of the Guanxie people under Tibetan Kunming also submitted.

sentences.zh: 贊普以其眾外潰，遂北寇靈、朔，陷麟州。

translations.literal: The tsenpo, because his forces had collapsed outward, then raided north into Ling and Shuo and captured Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With his southwestern forces in disarray, the Tibetan emperor turned north, raided Ling and Shuo, and took Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣使至成都府，令臯出兵深入蕃界。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong sent an envoy to Chengdu and ordered Gao to send troops deep into Tibetan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong sent envoys to Chengdu ordering Gao to drive deep into Tibetan territory.

sentences.zh: 臯乃令鎮靜軍使陳洎等統兵萬人出三奇路，威戎軍使崔堯臣兵千人出龍溪石門路南，維保二州兵馬使仇冕、保霸二州刺史董振等兵二千趨吐蕃維州城中，北路兵馬使邢玼等四千趨吐蕃棲雞、老翁城，都將高倜、王英俊兵二千趨故松州，隴東兵馬使元膺兵八千人出南道雅、邛、黎、巂路。

translations.literal: Gao then ordered Zhenjing Army commissioner Chen Ji and others to command ten thousand men out the Sanqi route; Weirong Army commissioner Cui Yaochan with one thousand men out the Longxi Shimen southern road; Wei and Bao prefectures' military commissioners Qiu Mian, Ba and Ba prefects Dong Zhen and others with two thousand toward Tibetan Weizhou city; northern-route military commissioner Xing Qi and others with four thousand toward Tibetan Qiji and Laoweng cities; commanders Gao Tong and Wang Yingjun with two thousand toward old Song Prefecture; Longdong military commissioner Yuan Ying with eight thousand out the southern route through Ya, Qiong, Li, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Zhenjing commissioner Chen Ji with ten thousand men along the Sanqi route; Weirong commissioner Cui Yaochan with a thousand along the Longxi Shimen road; Qiu Mian and the prefects of Wei and Ba with two thousand against Weizhou; Xing Qi with four thousand against Qiji and Laoweng; Gao Tong and Wang Yingjun with two thousand toward old Songzhou; and Yuan Ying with eight thousand along the southern Ya–Qiong–Li–Xi corridor.

sentences.zh: 又令鎮南軍使韋良金兵一千三百續進，雅州經略使路惟明等兵三千趨吐蕃租、松等城，黎州經略使王有道兵二千人過大渡河，深入蕃界，巂州經略使陳孝陽、兵馬使何大海、韋義等及磨些蠻、東蠻二部落主苴那時等兵四千進攻昆明城、諾濟城。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhennan Army commissioner Wei Liangjin with thirteen hundred to follow up; Ya Prefecture pacification commissioner Lu Weiming and others with three thousand toward Tibetan Zu and Song cities; Li Prefecture pacification commissioner Wang Youdao with two thousand to cross the Dadu River and penetrate deep into Tibetan territory; Xi Prefecture pacification commissioner Chen Xiaoyang, military commissioners He Dahai and Wei Yi, and the Mosuo and Eastern Barbarian chieftain Ju Nashi and others with four thousand to attack Kunming City and Nuoji City.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhennan commissioner Wei Liangjin with thirteen hundred as follow-up; Lu Weiming with three thousand against Zu and Song; Wang Youdao with two thousand across the Dadu into Tibetan lands; and Chen Xiaoyang, He Dahai, Wei Yi, and the Mosuo and Eastern Barbarian chief Ju Nashi with four thousand against Kunming and Nuoji.

sentences.zh: 自八月出軍齊入，至十月破蕃兵十六萬，拔城七、軍鎮五、戶三千，擒生六千，斬首萬余級，遂進攻維州。

translations.literal: From the eighth month the armies marched out together; by the tenth month they had broken one hundred sixty thousand Tibetan troops, taken seven cities, five army posts, three thousand households, captured six thousand alive, and beheaded more than ten thousand, then advanced to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The columns marched out together in the eighth month; by the tenth they had shattered a reported 160,000 Tibetan troops, taken seven cities and five garrisons, three thousand households, six thousand prisoners, and more than ten thousand heads, and pressed on to besiege Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 救軍再至，轉戰千里，蕃軍連敗。

translations.literal: Relief armies came again and again; fighting shifted over a thousand li and the Tibetan army suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns arrived again and again, battles ranged a thousand li, and the Tibetans lost every engagement.

sentences.zh: 於是寇靈、朔之眾引而南下，贊普遣論莽熱以內大相兼東境五道節度兵馬都群牧大使，率雜虜十萬而來解維州之圍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the forces that had raided Ling and Shuo turned south; the tsenpo sent Lun Mangre as inner chief minister concurrently eastern five-circuit military commissioner and overall herds commissioner, leading a hundred thousand mixed barbarians to relieve the siege of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army that had raided Ling and Shuo now swung south; the tsenpo sent Lun Mangre, inner chief minister and eastern frontier commander, with a hundred thousand mixed auxiliaries to lift the siege of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀師萬人據險設伏以待之，先出千人挑戰。

translations.literal: Ten thousand Shu troops held difficult ground and set an ambush to await them, first sending out a thousand men to provoke battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Shu troops took up a strong position in ambush and first sent out a thousand men to bait the enemy.

sentences.zh: 莽熱見我師之少，悉眾追之。

translations.literal: Mangre, seeing how few our troops were, pursued with his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how small the Tang detachment was, Mangre committed his whole army to the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 發伏掩擊，鼓噪雷駭，蕃兵自潰，生擒論莽熱，虜眾十萬，殲夷者半。

translations.literal: The ambush sprang forth in a masked attack; drums and shouts thundered like lightning; the Tibetan troops collapsed of themselves; Lun Mangre was captured alive; of the hundred thousand enemy, half were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden troops struck; drums and war cries rolled like thunder; the Tibetan line collapsed; Lun Mangre was taken alive; of his hundred thousand men, half were killed or scattered.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，遣使獻論莽熱於朝；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year an envoy was sent to present Lun Mangre at court;
translations.idiomatic: That October Gao sent Lun Mangre to the capital as a captive;

sentences.zh: 德宗數而釋之，賜第於崇仁裏。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong rebuked him and then released him, granting a residence in Chongren Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong lectured him, then set him free and gave him a house in Chongren Lane.

sentences.zh: 臯以功加檢校司徒，兼中書令，封南康郡王。

translations.literal: For his merit Gao was promoted to acting grand mentor, concurrently director of the Imperial Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For these victories Gao was made acting grand mentor and director of the Imperial Secretariat and enfeoffed as Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Gao was further made acting grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Gao was further appointed acting grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 順宗久疾，不能臨朝聽政，宦者李忠言、侍棋待詔王叔文、侍書待詔王伾等三人頗幹國政，高下在心。

translations.literal: Shunzong had long been ill and could not attend court to hear government; the eunuch Li Zhongyan, chess attendant Wang Shuwen, and calligraphy attendant Wang Pi—the three of them—handled state affairs to a considerable degree, with promotion and demotion at their whim.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong had been ill for years and could not preside over court; the eunuch Li Zhongyan, chess attendant Wang Shuwen, and calligraphy attendant Wang Pi largely ran the government, raising and lowering officials as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 臯乃遣支度副使劉辟使於京師，辟私謁王叔文曰：「太尉使致誠於足下，若能致某都領劍南三川，必有以相酬；

translations.literal: Gao then sent revenue vice commissioner Liu Pi on a mission to the capital; Pi privately visited Wang Shuwen and said, "The Grand Preceptor sends his sincerity to you; if you can secure for me command of the three circuits of Jiannan, there will certainly be reward;
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent his revenue vice commissioner Liu Pi to the capital; Pi sought a private audience with Wang Shuwen and said, "The Grand Preceptor sends his regards: if you can secure command of the three Jiannan circuits for him, he will repay you handsomely;

sentences.zh: 如不留意，亦有以奉報。」

translations.literal: if you do not heed this, there will also be means of repayment."
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse, he has other ways to settle the account."

sentences.zh: 叔文大怒，將斬辟以徇；

translations.literal: Shuwen was greatly angered and was about to behead Pi as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen flew into a rage and was about to execute Pi as a public warning;

sentences.zh: 韋執誼固止之，辟乃私去。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi firmly stopped him, and Pi then slipped away in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi held him back, and Pi slipped away.

sentences.zh: 臯知王叔文人情不附，又知與韋執誼有隙，自以大臣可議社稷大計，乃上表請皇太子監國，曰：「臣聞上承宗廟，下鎮黎元，永固無疆，莫先儲兩。

translations.literal: Gao knew that Wang Shuwen lacked popular support and also knew he was at odds with Wei Zhiyi; considering himself a great minister who might discuss the state's great plans, he submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince supervise the state, saying, "Your servant has heard that in inheriting the ancestral temples above and securing the black-haired people below, to secure eternal stability nothing comes before the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Shuwen lacked support and was at odds with Wei Zhiyi, Gao judged that as a frontier statesman he could weigh in on the fate of the dynasty and memorialized asking the crown prince to supervise the realm: "I have heard that to uphold the ancestral shrines above and steady the people below, nothing secures the realm like a firm succession.

sentences.zh: 伏聞聖明以山陵未祔，哀毀逾制，心勞萬幾，伏計旬月之間，未甚痊復。

translations.literal: I have heard that Your Sageliness, because the imperial tomb has not yet been enshrined, has exceeded the mourning regulations in grief and toil, and labors over the myriad affairs of state; I venture to estimate that within ten days or a month you have not yet fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that Your Majesty, with the late emperor's tomb not yet enshrined, mourns beyond the prescribed limits while bearing the weight of ten thousand affairs, and I fear full recovery may still be weeks away.

sentences.zh: 皇太子睿質已長，淑問日彰，四海之心，實所倚賴。

translations.literal: The crown prince's wise substance has already matured, his fine reputation grows daily, and the hearts of the four seas truly rely upon him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is grown in wisdom and reputation; the empire's hopes already rest on him.

sentences.zh: 伏望權令皇太子監撫庶政，以俟聖躬痊平，一日萬幾，免令壅滯。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will temporarily order the crown prince to oversee and comfort the common administration, to await Your Sagely Person's recovery; then the myriad affairs of a single day will not be allowed to stagnate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the crown prince be empowered to oversee daily government until Your Majesty is well again, so the business of the realm does not stall."

sentences.zh: 又上皇太子箋曰：

translations.literal: He also submitted a letter to the crown prince, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the crown prince a private letter:

sentences.zh: 殿下體重離之德，當儲貳之重，所以克昌九廟，式固萬方，天下安危，系於殿下。

translations.literal: Your Highness embodies the virtue of Heavy Brightness and bears the weight of the heir apparent; thereby the nine temples may flourish and the ten thousand regions be secured—the safety and peril of the realm hang upon Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness embodies the heir's virtue and bears the weight of succession; on you depend the prosperity of the ancestral shrines, the stability of the realm, and the safety of the empire.

sentences.zh: 臯位居將相，誌切匡扶，先朝獎知，早承恩顧。

translations.literal: Gao stands in the ranks of generals and ministers, his will set on aiding and supporting; the former court praised and knew him, and he early received gracious regard.
translations.idiomatic: I stand among your generals and ministers, resolved to serve you faithfully; the late emperor honored me, and I have long enjoyed imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 人臣之分，知無不為，願上答眷私，罄輸肝鬲。

translations.literal: The duty of a subject is that where he knows, there is nothing he will not do; I wish to answer your private favor above and pour out my liver and spleen entirely.
translations.idiomatic: A subject's duty is to act on whatever he knows; I wish to repay your trust and lay bare my utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 伏以聖上嗣膺鴻業，睿哲英明，攀感先朝，誌存孝理。

translations.literal: I submit that the sage emperor succeeding to the great enterprise is wise, perceptive, and brilliant, clinging in feeling to the former court and keeping his will in filial governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your father succeeded to the great enterprise with wisdom and brilliance, cherishing the late emperor and devoted to filial rule.

sentences.zh: 諒闇之際，方委大臣，但付托偶失於善人，而參決多虧於公政。

translations.literal: In the period of sincere mourning he has just entrusted great ministers, but the commission has by chance fallen on unworthy men, and participation in decisions has largely failed public government.
translations.idiomatic: In his mourning he entrusted affairs to senior ministers, yet power has fallen by mischance into the wrong hands, and public government has suffered.

sentences.zh: 今群小得誌，隳紊紀綱，官以勢遷，政由情改，朋黨交構，熒惑宸聰。

translations.literal: Now petty men have gained their aim, destroying and disordering statutes and discipline; offices shift by power, government changes by private feeling; cliques weave plots and dazzle the imperial ear.
translations.idiomatic: Now petty men have had their way, tearing down law and order, trading offices for favor, bending policy to private whim, forming factions, and misleading the throne.

sentences.zh: 樹置腹心，遍於貴位；

translations.literal: They plant trusted confidants throughout exalted posts;
translations.idiomatic: They plant their intimates in every high post;

sentences.zh: 潛結左右，難在蕭墻。

translations.literal: they secretly bind those at the emperor's side—the peril lies within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: they secretly bind the emperor's attendants—the danger is within the palace itself.

sentences.zh: 國賦散於權門，王稅不入天府，褻慢無忌，高下在心。

translations.literal: National levies are scattered among powerful houses; royal taxes do not enter the imperial treasury; irreverence knows no restraint; promotion and demotion rest in their hearts alone.
translations.idiomatic: State revenue is diverted to powerful houses, royal taxes never reach the treasury, insolence goes unchecked, and they raise or ruin men at will.

sentences.zh: 貨賄流聞，遷轉失敘，先聖屏黜贓犯之類，鹹擢居省寺之間。

translations.literal: Bribes circulate openly; transfers lose proper order; men whom the former sage banished as corrupt offenders are all promoted into the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Bribery is an open secret, appointments ignore seniority, and men the late emperor banished for corruption now sit in the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 至令忠臣隕涕，正人結舌，遐邇痛心，人知不可。

translations.literal: It has come to the point that loyal ministers shed tears, upright men seal their tongues, far and near are heartsick, and everyone knows this cannot continue.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers weep, upright officials dare not speak, and all who near and far see it know the situation cannot stand.

sentences.zh: 伏恐奸雄乘便，因此謀動干戈，危殿下之家邦，傾太宗之王業。

translations.literal: I fear treacherous heroes will seize the opportunity, plot accordingly, and stir weapons of war, endangering Your Highness's house and state and overturning Taizong's royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that schemers will seize the moment, raise arms, endanger your house and throne, and overturn the empire Taizong built.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太宗櫛沐風雨，經營廟朝，將垂二百年，欲及千萬祀；

translations.literal: I submit that Taizong, bathed in wind and rain, built the temple-altars of the court, intending nearly two hundred years and desiring to reach a thousand myriad sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong endured wind and rain to build this dynasty for ages to come, intending it to last centuries and ten thousand generations;

sentences.zh: 而一朝使叔文奸佞之徒，侮弄朝政，恣其胸臆，坐致傾危。

translations.literal: yet in a single morning to let Shuwen and such treacherous flatterers mock and toy with court government, indulge their breasts and bellies, and thereby bring collapse and peril sitting still.
translations.idiomatic: yet in a single reign men like Shuwen mock the government, indulge their whims, and risk bringing it all down.

sentences.zh: 臣每思之，痛心疾首！

translations.literal: Whenever your servant thinks of it, his heart aches and his head pains!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of it, grief pierces me to the core!

sentences.zh: 伏望殿下斥逐群小，委任賢良，忄妻々血誠，輸寫於此！

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Highness will drive out the petty crowd, entrust the worthy and good, and with earnest blood-sincerity pour it all forth here!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to drive out these petty men, entrust the worthy, and accept the heartfelt loyalty I pour out here!

sentences.zh: 太子優令答之。

translations.literal: The crown prince graciously ordered a reply.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince graciously sent a reply.

sentences.zh: 而裴均、嚴綬箋表繼至，由是政歸太子，盡逐伾文之黨。

translations.literal: Then memorial letters from Pei Jun and Yan Shou arrived in succession; thereby government returned to the crown prince and the faction of Pi and Wen was entirely driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from Pei Jun and Yan Shou followed, and power passed to the crown prince, who expelled the entire Wang Pi–Wang Shuwen faction.

sentences.zh: 是歲，暴疾卒，時年六十一，贈太師，廢朝五日。

translations.literal: That year he died suddenly of illness at the age of sixty-one; he was posthumously made grand preceptor and court mourning was suspended for five days.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died suddenly of illness at sixty-one; the court posthumously named him grand preceptor and suspended audiences for five days.

sentences.zh: 臯在蜀二十一年，重賦斂以事月進，卒致蜀土虛竭，時論非之。

translations.literal: Gao was in Shu for twenty-one years, levying heavy taxes to supply monthly tribute, and in the end caused Shu to be drained empty; contemporary opinion criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao governed Shu for twenty-one years, imposing heavy taxes to fund his monthly gifts to the throne until the province was exhausted, and contemporaries condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 其從事累官稍崇者，則奏為屬郡刺史，或又署在府幕，多不令還朝，蓋不欲泄所為於闕下故也。

translations.literal: Those of his staff who rose somewhat in rank he would memorialize as prefects of subordinate commanderies, or again appoint in the headquarters staff, mostly not allowing them to return to court—presumably because he did not wish to leak his doings below the imperial gates.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members who rose in rank he posted as prefects in outlying districts or kept in his own headquarters, rarely allowing them back to the capital, lest his dealings there become known.

sentences.zh: 故劉辟因臯故態，圖不軌以求三川，歷階之作，蓋有由然。

translations.literal: Therefore Liu Pi, following Gao's old ways, plotted irregularity to seek the three circuits; his climbing the steps had its reasons.
translations.idiomatic: It was in this tradition that Liu Pi, following Gao's example, plotted rebellion to seize the three circuits—his ambition had deep roots.

sentences.zh: 臯兄聿，時為國子司業，劉辟與盧文若據西川叛，臯侄行式，先娶文若妹，而聿不奏。

translations.literal: Gao's elder brother Yu was at the time vice director of the Directorate of Education; when Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo held West Sichuan in rebellion, Gao's nephew Xingshi had earlier married Wenruo's younger sister, yet Yu did not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's elder brother Yu was vice director of the Directorate of Education; when Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo rebelled in West Sichuan, Gao's nephew Xingshi had married Wenruo's sister, yet Yu never reported the connection.

sentences.zh: 既收行式，以其妻沒官，詔御史臺按聿，聿下獄。

translations.literal: Once Xingshi was taken, his wife was confiscated to the state; an edict ordered the Censorate to investigate Yu, and Yu was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingshi was arrested, his wife was confiscated; the Censorate was ordered to investigate Yu, and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 有司以行式妻在遠，不與兄同情，不當連坐，詔歸行式妻而釋聿。

translations.literal: The authorities held that Xingshi's wife was far away and did not share her brother's intent, and should not be punished by association; an edict returned Xingshi's wife and released Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities ruled that Xingshi's wife, living far away, could not have shared her brother's guilt and should not be punished with him; the court returned her to Xingshi and released Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉辟者，貞元中進士擢第，宏詞登科，韋臯辟為從事，累遷至御史中丞、支度副使。

translations.literal: Liu Pi, in the Zhenyuan era, passed the presented scholar examination and the macro-elocution examination; Wei Gao recruited him as staff officer, and he was repeatedly promoted to vice censor-in-chief and revenue vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi passed the civil service and macro-elocution examinations in the Zhenyuan era; Wei Gao took him on as staff and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief and revenue vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年八月，韋臯卒，辟自為西川節度留後，率成都將校上表請降節鉞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongzhen, when Wei Gao died, Pi made himself West Sichuan military governor's acting rear administrator and led Chengdu generals and officers in a memorial requesting the grant of the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongzhen 1, when Wei Gao died, Liu Pi named himself acting military governor of West Sichuan and led Chengdu's officers in a memorial requesting formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不許，除給事中，便令赴闕。

translations.literal: The court did not consent, but appointed him supervising censor and ordered him to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused his request but named him supervising censor and ordered him to report to the capital.

sentences.zh: 辟不奉詔。

translations.literal: Pi did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi defied the order.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗初即位，以無事息人為務，遂授辟檢校工部尚書，充劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xianzong had just ascended the throne and made peace and resting the people his task; he therefore appointed Pi acting minister of works and military governor of Jiannan West.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had just taken the throne and wished to avoid war, so he appointed Liu Pi acting minister of works and military governor of Jiannan West.

sentences.zh: 辟益兇悖，出不臣之言，而求都統三川，與同幕盧文若相善，欲以文若為東川節度使，遂舉兵圍梓州。

translations.literal: Pi grew ever more fierce and rebellious, uttered disloyal words, and sought overall command of the three circuits; he was close to his fellow staff member Lu Wenruo and wished to make Wenruo East Sichuan military governor, then raised troops and besieged Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pi grew bolder, spoke treasonously, demanded command of all three circuits, and—close to his colleague Lu Wenruo, whom he wanted as East Sichuan governor—raised an army and besieged Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗難於用兵，宰相杜黃裳奏：「劉辟一狂蹶書生耳，王師鼓行而俘之，兵不血刃。

translations.literal: Xianzong was reluctant to use troops; chief minister Du Huangchang memorialized, "Liu Pi is only a mad, reckless scholar; the imperial army can march and capture him without blades drawing blood.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong hesitated to send troops, but Chief Minister Du Huangchang argued, "Liu Pi is nothing but a reckless scholar; the imperial army can march on him and take him without a fight.

sentences.zh: 臣知神策軍使高崇文，驍果可任，舉必成功。」

translations.literal: Your servant knows Shence Army commissioner Gao Chongwen, brave and capable, whom if recommended will certainly succeed."
translations.idiomatic: I know the Shence commander Gao Chongwen—fierce and reliable—and if you send him, he will succeed.

sentences.zh: 帝數日方從之。

translations.literal: Only after several days did the emperor follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took several days to agree.

sentences.zh: 於是令高崇文、李元奕將神策京西行營兵相續進發，令與嚴礪、李康掎角相應以討之，仍許其自新。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Gao Chongwen and Li Yuanyi to lead Shence western capital campaign troops to advance in succession, to coordinate with Yan Li and Li Kang in pincer response to attack him, and still allowed him to reform.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Gao Chongwen and Li Yuanyi to march the Shence western capital troops forward in stages, coordinating with Yan Li and Li Kang in a pincer attack, while still offering Pi a chance to submit.

sentences.zh: 元和元年正月，崇文出師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanhe, Chongwen took the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanhe 1, Gao Chongwen took the field.

sentences.zh: 三月，收復東川。

translations.literal: In the third month East Sichuan was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By the third month East Sichuan had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict was then issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 朕聞皇祖玄元之誡曰：「兵者，兇器也，不得已而用之。」

translations.literal: We have heard our imperial ancestor the Mysterious Primeval's admonition: "Arms are baleful instruments, to be used only when there is no alternative."
translations.idiomatic: Our imperial ancestor the Mysterious Primeval taught: "Weapons are instruments of violence, to be used only when there is no other choice.

sentences.zh: 恭惟聖謨，常所祗服。

translations.literal: We respectfully hold this sage counsel and constantly revere and follow it.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that sacred teaching in reverence and live by it.

sentences.zh: 故惟文誥有所不至，誠信有所未孚，始務安人，必能忍恥，朕之此誌，亦可明征。

translations.literal: Therefore when civil edicts did not reach everywhere and sincerity and trust had not yet won hearts, we first sought to settle the people and were able to bear humiliation—this resolve of ours may also be clearly seen.
translations.idiomatic: When persuasion and trust had not yet won the day, we first sought to pacify the people and bore humiliation rather than strike—our intent in this is plain.

sentences.zh: 近者德宗皇帝舉柔服之規，授宰衡之傑，弘我廟勝，遂康巴、庸，故得南詔入貢，西戎寢患。

translations.literal: Recently Emperor Dezong raised the policy of gentle submission, entrusted outstanding chief ministers, expanded our temple victories, and thereby secured Ba and Yong; thus Nanzhao came to offer tribute and western barbarians laid their troubles to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Dezong the court pursued conciliation, entrusted great ministers, and secured Ba and Yong, bringing Nanzhao to tribute and quieting the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 成績始究，元臣喪亡，劉辟乘此變故，坐邀符節。

translations.literal: When achievements had just been completed and the great minister died, Liu Pi seized this change and sat waiting to demand the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: Just as those achievements were won and Wei Gao died, Liu Pi seized the moment to demand the command baton for himself.

sentences.zh: 朕以成狂命者雖乖於理體，從權便者所冀於輯寧，竟乖卿士之謀，遂允幸求之誌。

translations.literal: We considered that fulfilling a mad command, though at odds with principle, might serve expedient peace; going against our ministers' counsel, we granted his importunate wish.
translations.idiomatic: Though indulging his presumption violated principle, we hoped expedience would buy peace, and against our ministers' advice we granted his request.

sentences.zh: 朕之於辟，恩亦弘矣。

translations.literal: Our grace toward Pi was already great.
translations.idiomatic: Our favor toward Liu Pi was already generous.

sentences.zh: 曾不知恩，負牛羊之力，飽則逾兇；

translations.literal: He did not know gratitude, bore the strength of oxen and sheep, and once sated grew ever more vicious;
translations.idiomatic: He showed no gratitude, fed like a beast on our bounty, and once full grew only more savage;

sentences.zh: 畜梟獍之心，馴之益悖。

translations.literal: he harbored the heart of an owl or fledgling beast, and the more he was tamed the more rebellious he became.
translations.idiomatic: he nursed an owl's heart in his breast, and the more we indulged him the more defiant he grew.

sentences.zh: 誑惑士伍，圍逼梓州；

translations.literal: he deceived and led astray the soldiers, besieged and pressed Zizhou;
translations.idiomatic: He misled the troops and besieged Zizhou;

sentences.zh: 誘陷戎臣，塞絕劍路。

translations.literal: he enticed and trapped frontier officials and blocked the Sword Pass road.
translations.idiomatic: he lured frontier officials into treason and cut the roads into Shu.

sentences.zh: 師徒所至，燒劫無遺，幹紀之辜，擢發難數。

translations.literal: Wherever his armies went, burning and plunder left nothing; crimes against discipline, if counted hair by hair, would be beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever his armies marched they burned and looted without mercy, and his violations of law are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 朕為人司牧，字彼黎元，如辟之罪，非朕敢舍，可削奪在身官爵。

translations.literal: We, as shepherd of the people, cherish the black-haired masses; for crimes such as Pi's, we dare not pardon—his current offices and ranks may be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: As shepherd of the people we cannot forgive crimes such as his; let his offices and titles be stripped away.

sentences.zh: 六月，崇文破鹿頭關，進收漢州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Chongwen broke Lutou Pass and advanced to recover Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Gao Chongwen stormed Lutou Pass and took Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，崇文收成都府。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chongwen recovered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he captured Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 劉辟以數十騎遁走，投水不死；

translations.literal: Liu Pi fled with several dozen horsemen, threw himself into the water but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi fled with a few dozen horsemen, threw himself into the river but survived;

sentences.zh: 騎將酈定進入水，擒辟於成都府西洋灌田。

translations.literal: cavalry officer Li Dingjin entered the water and captured Pi in the western irrigation fields outside Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: cavalry officer Li Dingjin went in after him and seized Liu Pi in the irrigation fields west of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 盧文若先自刃其妻子，然後縋石投江，失其屍。

translations.literal: Lu Wenruo first killed his wife and children with his own blade, then tied a stone and cast himself into the river; his corpse was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenruo first killed his wife and children, then weighted himself with a stone and drowned in the river; his body was never found.

sentences.zh: 辟檻送京師，在路飲食自若，以為不當死。

translations.literal: Pi was sent to the capital in a cage cart; on the road he ate and drank as usual, believing he ought not to die.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi was sent to the capital in a cage cart, eating and drinking calmly along the way because he believed he would not be executed.

sentences.zh: 及至京西臨臯驛，左右神策兵士迎之，以帛系首及手足，曳而入，乃驚曰：「何至於是？」

translations.literal: When he reached the Lin'gao post west of the capital, left and right Shence soldiers received him, bound his head and hands and feet with silk, and dragged him in; he then cried in alarm, "How could it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Lin'gao post west of the capital, Shence guards bound his head and limbs with silk and dragged him inside; only then did he cry out in alarm, "How could it come to this?

sentences.zh: 或紿之曰：「國法當爾，無憂也。」

translations.literal: Someone deceived him, saying, "State law requires this; do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Someone lied to him, "That is what the law requires—do not worry."

sentences.zh: 是日，詔曰：「劉辟生於士族，敢蓄梟心，驅劫蜀人，拒扞王命。

translations.literal: That day an edict said, "Liu Pi was born into the gentry class yet dared to harbor an owl's heart, drove and plundered the people of Shu, and resisted the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict declared, "Born to the gentry, Liu Pi yet harbored treason, drove the people of Shu into rebellion, and defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 肆其狂逆，詿誤一州，俾我黎元，肝腦塗地。

translations.literal: He indulged his mad rebellion, misled a whole prefecture, and caused our black-haired people to have their livers and brains smeared on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He ran riot, misled a whole province, and brought ruin on the people.

sentences.zh: 賊將崔綱等同惡相扇，至死不回，咸宜伏辜，以正刑典。

translations.literal: Rebel generals such as Cui Gang fanned one another's evil and would not turn back even unto death; all should pay the penalty to rectify the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel officers such as Cui Gang incited one another and would not relent; all must pay with their lives under the law.

sentences.zh: 劉辟男超郎等九人，並處斬。」

translations.literal: Liu Pi's sons Chaolang and the other nine persons were all executed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi's son Chaolang and eight others were all executed."

sentences.zh: 辟入京城，上御興安樓受俘馘，令中使於樓下詰辟反狀。

translations.literal: When Pi entered the capital, the emperor ascended Xing'an Tower to receive the captive and severed heads, and ordered a palace envoy below the tower to interrogate Pi on the facts of his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi entered the capital, the emperor mounted Xing'an Tower to receive the captive and ordered a palace envoy below to question him about his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 辟曰：「臣不敢反，五院子弟為惡，臣不能制。」

translations.literal: Pi said, "Your servant did not dare rebel; the sons of the Fifth Courtyard did evil, and your servant could not control them."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi said, "I never rebelled; the men of the Fifth Courtyard ran wild, and I could not control them.

sentences.zh: 又遣詰之曰：「朕遣中使送旌節官告，何故不受？」

translations.literal: He was again sent to question him: "We dispatched a palace envoy to deliver the command baton and appointment documents—why did you not accept them?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy pressed him again: "The throne sent you the command baton and appointment—why did you refuse them?"

sentences.zh: 辟乃伏罪。

translations.literal: Pi then confessed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Liu Pi confess.

sentences.zh: 令獻太廟、郊社，徇於市，即日戮於子城西南隅。

translations.literal: He was ordered presented at the Grand Temple and suburban altars, displayed in the market, and that same day executed at the southwest corner of the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: He was presented at the ancestral temple and suburban altars, paraded through the market, and executed that same day at the southwest corner of the inner city.

sentences.zh: 初，辟嘗病，見諸問疾者來，皆以手據地，倒行入辟口，辟因礫裂食之；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Pi had been ill, he saw all who came to inquire after his health place their hands on the ground and crawl backward into Pi's mouth; Pi would then crush them with gravel and eat them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Pi fell ill, he dreamed that every visitor crawled backward on hands and feet into his mouth, where he crushed and devoured them;

sentences.zh: 惟盧文若至，則如平常。

translations.literal: only when Lu Wenruo came was it as usual.
translations.idiomatic: only when Lu Wenruo came did the dream proceed normally.

sentences.zh: 故尤與文若厚，竟以同惡俱赤族，不其怪歟！

translations.literal: Therefore he was especially close to Wenruo; in the end, for sharing evil they were both exterminated to the last clan—is it not strange!
translations.idiomatic: So he was especially close to Wenruo—and in the end both men and their clans were destroyed. Was that not an omen fulfilled?

sentences.zh: 張建封，字本立，兗州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jianfeng, courtesy name Benli, was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, whose courtesy name was Benli, came from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖仁範，洪州南昌縣令，貞元初贈鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Renfan was magistrate of Nanchang County in Hong Prefecture and was posthumously made prefect of Zheng Prefecture in the early Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Renfan had been magistrate of Nanchang in Hong Prefecture and was posthumously named prefect of Zheng in the early Zhenyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 父玠，少豪俠，輕財重士。

translations.literal: His father Jie in youth was bold and chivalrous, slighting wealth and valuing scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie had been a bold, generous youth who scorned wealth and honored men of talent.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，令偽將李庭偉率蕃兵脅下城邑，至魯郡；

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he ordered the false general Li Tingwei to lead barbarian troops to coerce the surrender of cities and towns, reaching Lu commandery;
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, his puppet general Li Tingwei led barbarian troops to coerce cities along the route as far as Lu commandery;

sentences.zh: 太守韓擇木具禮郊迎，置於郵館。

translations.literal: the prefect Han Zhemu received him with full rites in the suburban welcome and lodged him in the courier station.
translations.idiomatic: prefect Han Zhemu went out with full ceremony to receive him and lodged him in the courier station.

sentences.zh: 玠率鄉豪張貴、孫邑、段絳等集兵將殺之。

translations.literal: Jie led local worthies Zhang Gui, Sun Yi, Duan Jiang, and others to gather troops intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jie rallied local leaders Zhang Gui, Sun Yi, Duan Jiang, and others to raise troops and kill him.

sentences.zh: 擇木怯懦，大懼；

translations.literal: Zhemu was cowardly and greatly afraid;
translations.idiomatic: Zhemu was timid and terrified;

sentences.zh: 唯員外司兵張孚然其計，遂殺庭偉並其黨數十人，擇木方遣使奏聞。

translations.literal: only the extra bureau army officer Zhang Fu approved the plan; they then killed Tingwei and several dozen of his followers, after which Zhemu sent an envoy to report.
translations.idiomatic: only the army officer Zhang Fu backed the plan; they killed Tingwei and dozens of his men, and only then did Zhemu send word to the court.

sentences.zh: 擇木、張孚俱受官賞，玠因遊蕩江南，不言其功。

translations.literal: Zhemu and Zhang Fu both received offices and rewards; Jie, because he was wandering in the south of the Yangzi, did not speak of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhemu and Zhang Fu were both rewarded with offices, while Jie, wandering in the lower Yangzi, never claimed credit.

sentences.zh: 以建封貴，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: Because Jianfeng became eminent, Jie was posthumously made director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng rose to eminence, his father was posthumously named director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建封少頗屬文，好談論，慷慨負氣，以功名為己任。

translations.literal: Jianfeng in youth was rather skilled in letters, loved discussion, was generous and spirited, and took merit and fame as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jianfeng wrote well, loved debate, was bold and high-spirited, and made achievement his life's aim.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，李光弼鎮河南，時蘇、常等州草賊，寇掠郡邑，代宗遣中使馬日新與光弼將兵馬同征討之。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era Li Guangbi guarded Henan; at that time grassland bandits in Su, Chang, and other prefectures raided commandery cities; Emperor Daizong sent palace envoy Ma Rixin with Guangbi to lead troops together to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying era, while Li Guangbi held Henan, bandits in Su and Chang prefectures were raiding the countryside; Emperor Daizong sent the palace envoy Ma Rixin with Guangbi to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 建封乃見日新，自請說喻賊徒。

translations.literal: Jianfeng then visited Rixin and volunteered to persuade and instruct the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng sought out Ma Rixin and volunteered to talk the bandits into surrender.

sentences.zh: 日新從之，遂入虎窟、蒸裏等賊營，以利害禍福喻之。

translations.literal: Rixin agreed; he then entered the bandit camps at Huku and Zhengli and explained advantage, harm, disaster, and blessing to them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rixin agreed, and Jianfeng entered the camps at Huku and Zhengli to argue profit and loss, ruin and reward.

sentences.zh: 一夕，賊黨數千人並詣日新請降，遂悉放歸田裏。

translations.literal: In one night several thousand bandits all came to Rixin to request surrender, and they were all released to return to their fields.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night several thousand bandits came to Ma Rixin to surrender, and all were sent home to their farms.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，道州刺史裴虬薦建封於觀察使韋之晉，辟為參謀，奏授左清道兵曹，不樂吏役而去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dali, Daozhou prefect Pei Qiu recommended Jianfeng to observation commissioner Wei Zhijin, who recruited him as staff planner and memorialized to appoint him left Qingdao army registrar; disliking clerical service, he left.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Dali reign, Daozhou prefect Pei Qiu recommended him to observation commissioner Wei Zhijin, who took him on as staff and had him named army registrar; Jianfeng soon quit, disliking routine office work.

sentences.zh: 滑亳節度使令狐彰聞其名，辟之；

translations.literal: Huabo military governor Linghu Zhang heard his name and recruited him;
translations.idiomatic: Huabo military governor Linghu Zhang heard of him and recruited him;

sentences.zh: 彰既未曾朝覲，建封心不悅之，遂投刺於轉運使劉晏，自述其誌，不願仕於彰也。

translations.literal: since Zhang had never attended court, Jianfeng was displeased in heart and therefore presented his card to transport commissioner Liu Yan, stating his will that he did not wish to serve under Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: but Zhang had never come to court, which Jianfeng disliked; he therefore called on transport commissioner Liu Yan, explained his views, and said he would not serve under Zhang.

sentences.zh: 晏奏試大理評事，勾當軍務。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized to try him as Dali review official in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan had him tried out as a Dali review official handling military affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復罷歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he left office again.

sentences.zh: 建封素與馬燧友善，大歷十年，燧為河陽三城鎮遏使，辟為判官，奏授監察御史，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: Jianfeng had long been friendly with Ma Sui; in the tenth year of Dali, when Sui was Heyang Three Cities suppression commissioner, he recruited him as judge, memorialized to appoint him supervisory censor, and granted a crimson fish bag.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng had long been close to Ma Sui; in Dali 10, when Sui became commissioner for the Heyang Three Cities, he made Jianfeng his judge, secured him a supervisory censor's title, and gave him the crimson fish bag.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜反於梁、宋間，與田悅掎角，同為叛逆，燧與李忠臣同討平之，軍務多咨於建封。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao rebelled between Liang and Song, coordinated with Tian Yue in pincer fashion, and together became rebels; Sui and Li Zhongchen jointly suppressed and pacified them, and military affairs were largely consulted with Jianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled in the Liang–Song region in concert with Tian Yue, Ma Sui and Li Zhongchen crushed them together, consulting Jianfeng on most military decisions.

sentences.zh: 及燧為河東節度使，復奏建封為判官，特拜侍御史。

translations.literal: When Sui became Hedong military governor, he again memorialized Jianfeng as judge and specially appointed him attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui became Hedong military governor, he again named Jianfeng judge and specially appointed him attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 建中初，燧薦之於朝，楊炎將用為度支郎中，盧杞惡之，出為岳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Sui recommended him to court; Yang Yan was about to use him as revenue bureau director, but Lu Qi disliked him and sent him out as Yuezhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign Sui recommended him to court; Yang Yan meant to make him revenue bureau director, but Lu Qi disliked him and sent him out as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 時淮西節度使李希烈乘破滅梁崇義之勢，漸縱恣跋扈，壽州刺史崔昭數書疏往來。

translations.literal: At that time Huai West military governor Li Xilie, riding the momentum of destroying Liang Chongyi, gradually grew unrestrained and overbearing; Shouzhou prefect Cui Zhao exchanged numerous letters and memorials with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai West governor Li Xilie, emboldened by his defeat of Liang Chongyi, grew increasingly arrogant, and Shouzhou prefect Cui Zhao exchanged many letters with him.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少遊奏之，上遽召宰相令選壽州刺史。

translations.literal: Huainan military governor Chen Shaoyou memorialized this; the emperor hastily summoned the chief ministers and ordered them to choose a Shouzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan governor Chen Shaoyou reported this, and the emperor at once summoned the chief ministers to choose a new Shouzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 盧杞本惡建封，是日蒼黃，遂薦建封以代崔昭牧壽陽。

translations.literal: Lu Qi had originally disliked Jianfeng, but that day in haste he recommended Jianfeng to replace Cui Zhao in governing Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi had always disliked Jianfeng, but in the emergency of that day he recommended him to replace Cui Zhao at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 李希烈稱兵，寇陷汝州，擒李元平，擊走胡德信、唐漢臣等，又摧破哥舒曜於襄城，連陷鄭、汴等州，李勉棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Li Xilie raised arms, invaded and captured Ruzhou, seized Li Yuanping, routed Hu Dexin, Tang Hanchen, and others, also crushed Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng, and in succession took Zheng, Bian, and other prefectures; Li Mian abandoned his city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie took the field, captured Ruzhou, seized Li Yuanping, routed Hu Dexin and Tang Hanchen, crushed Geshu Yao at Xiangcheng, and swept through Zheng and Bian; Li Mian abandoned his post and fled.

sentences.zh: 涇師內逆，駕幸奉天，賊鋒益盛。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou troops mutinied within, the imperial carriage went to Fengtian, and the rebels' momentum grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhou mutiny broke out, the emperor fled to Fengtian, and rebel power surged.

sentences.zh: 淮南陳少遊潛通希烈，尋稱偽號，改元，遣將楊豐賫偽赦書二道，令送少遊及建封。

translations.literal: Huainan's Chen Shaoyou secretly communicated with Xilie, soon declared a false title, changed the era name, and sent the general Yang Feng bearing two false amnesty documents to deliver to Shaoyou and Jianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan secretly colluded with Xilie, soon declared himself emperor under a new reign title, and sent Yang Feng with two forged amnesties for Shaoyou and Jianfeng.

sentences.zh: 至壽州，建封縛楊豐徇於軍中。

translations.literal: When he reached Shou Prefecture, Jianfeng bound Yang Feng and displayed him through the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Shou Prefecture, Jianfeng bound Yang Feng and paraded him before the troops.

sentences.zh: 適會中使自行在及使江南回者同至，建封集眾對中使斬豐於通衢，封偽赦書送行在，遠近震駭。

translations.literal: It happened that palace envoys from the imperial presence and those returning from missions to the south of the Yangzi arrived together; Jianfeng assembled the masses, and before the envoys beheaded Feng in the open thoroughfare, sealed the false amnesty documents, and sent them to the imperial presence—the near and far were shaken in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys from the emperor's camp and from missions to the south happened to arrive together; Jianfeng assembled the troops, executed Yang Feng in public before them, sealed the forged amnesties, and sent them to the emperor—news that stunned the region.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊聞之，既怒且懼。

translations.literal: When Chen Shaoyou heard of it, he was both angry and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou was furious and terrified when he heard.

sentences.zh: 建封乃具奏少遊與希烈往來事狀。

translations.literal: Jianfeng then submitted a full memorial on the circumstances of Shaoyou's dealings with Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng then memorialized in full on Chen Shaoyou's dealings with Xilie.

sentences.zh: 希烈又偽署其黨杜少誠為淮南節度使，令先平壽州，趣江都。

translations.literal: Xilie also falsely appointed his follower Du Shaocheng Huainan military governor, ordering him first to pacify Shou Prefecture and hurry to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie also named his follower Du Shaocheng puppet governor of Huainan and ordered him to take Shou Prefecture first, then march on Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 建封令其將賀蘭元均、邵怡等守霍丘秋柵。

translations.literal: Jianfeng ordered his generals Helan Yuanjun, Shao Yi, and others to hold the Qiuchai stockade at Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng sent his generals Helan Yuanjun and Shao Yi to hold the autumn stockade at Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 少誠竟不能侵軼，乃南掠蘄、黃等州，又為伊慎所挫衄。

translations.literal: Shaocheng in the end could not break through, then raided south into Qi, Huang, and other prefectures, and was again checked and defeated by Yi Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shaocheng could not break through, turned south to raid Qi and Huang, and was beaten back by Yi Shen.

sentences.zh: 尋加建封兼御史中丞、本州團練使。

translations.literal: Soon Jianfeng was additionally made vice censor-in-chief and regimental commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng was soon also named vice censor-in-chief and regimental commissioner of his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，陳少遊憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Chen Shaoyou died of grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Chen Shaoyou died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 興元元年十二月，乃加兼御史大夫，充濠壽廬三州都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Xingyuan he was further made concurrent censor-in-chief and overall regimental and observation commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Xingyuan 1 he was also made censor-in-chief and overall regimental and observation commissioner of Hao, Shou, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 於是大修緝城池，悉心綏撫，遠近悅附，自是威望益重。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly repaired city walls and moats, devoted himself to soothing and comforting, and near and far gladly attached themselves; from this his prestige grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the walls and devoted himself to governing well; people near and far rallied to him, and his prestige grew.

sentences.zh: 李希烈選兇黨精悍者率勁卒以攻建封，曠日持久，無所克獲而去。

translations.literal: Li Xilie selected fierce party members and led crack troops to attack Jianfeng; the campaign dragged on for days without gain, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie sent picked troops under his fiercest officers against Jianfeng, but after a long stalemate they withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 及希烈平，進階封，賜一子正員官。

translations.literal: When Xilie was pacified, Jianfeng's noble rank was advanced and one son was granted a regular official post.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilie's defeat, Jianfeng's noble rank was raised and one of his sons was given a regular court post.

sentences.zh: 初，建中年，李涓以徐州歸附。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jianzhong era, Li Juan brought Xuzhou back to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong era, Li Juan had brought Xuzhou back to the Tang side.

sentences.zh: 涓尋卒，其後高承宗父子、獨孤華相繼為刺史。

translations.literal: Juan soon died; afterward Gao Chengzong father and son and Dugu Hua in succession became prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Juan soon died, and Gao Chengzong and his son, then Dugu Hua, succeeded one another as prefect.

sentences.zh: 為賊侵削，貧困不能自存；

translations.literal: They were whittled away by rebels and were so impoverished they could not sustain themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Rebel wars had stripped the region bare until it could barely sustain itself;

sentences.zh: 又咽喉要地，據江淮運路，朝廷思擇重臣以鎮者久之。

translations.literal: moreover it was a vital throat-point controlling the Yangzi–Huai transport route, and the court had long pondered choosing a weighty minister to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: yet it was a strategic choke point on the Yangzi–Huai transport route, and the court had long sought a strong minister to hold it.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，以建封為徐州刺史，兼御史大夫、徐泗濠節度、支度營田觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan, Jianfeng was made Xuzhou prefect, concurrently censor-in-chief, Xu-Si-Hao military governor, and revenue, agricultural colony, and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 he was made prefect of Xuzhou, concurrently censor-in-chief, military governor of Xu–Si–Hao, and revenue, agricultural colony, and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既創置軍伍，建封觸事躬親；

translations.literal: Once he had newly established the army, Jianfeng personally attended to every matter;
translations.idiomatic: After organizing the army, he attended to every matter in person;

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，容納人過誤，而按據綱紀，不妄曲法貸人。

translations.literal: his nature was generous and broad, he tolerated men's faults and errors, yet he upheld discipline and statutes and did not lightly bend the law to pardon people.
translations.idiomatic: he was generous and tolerant of faults, yet upheld discipline and never bent the law to favor anyone.

sentences.zh: 每言事，忠義感激，人皆畏悅。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke on affairs, loyalty and righteousness stirred the feelings, and all both feared and were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke, his loyalty and passion moved everyone to respect and admiration.

sentences.zh: 七年，進位檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to acting minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to acting minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was made acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made acting right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，入覲京師，德宗禮遇加等，特以雙日開延英召對，又令朝參入大夫班，以示殊寵。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year he entered the capital to pay court; Dezong's courtesy exceeded the norm, specially opening Yanying on double days for audience, and also ordering him to attend court in the great ministers' rank to show special favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year he came to court; Emperor Dezong received him with exceptional honor, summoned him to Yanying Hall on special days, and had him take his place in the great ministers' rank at audience.

sentences.zh: 建封賦《朝天行》一章上獻，賜名馬珍玩頗厚。

translations.literal: Jianfeng composed one chapter of "Song of Going to Court" and presented it; he was granted famous horses and precious objects in considerable measure.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a poem, "Journey to Court," and received fine horses and rich gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 時宦者主宮中市買，謂之宮市，抑買人物，稍不如本估。

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs controlled palace market purchases, called "palace market"; they forced purchases of goods at prices somewhat below original estimates.
translations.idiomatic: At the time eunuchs controlled palace purchases—the so-called palace market—forcing merchants to sell below fair price.

sentences.zh: 末年不復行文書，置白望數十百人於兩市及要鬧坊曲，閱人所賣物；

translations.literal: In his later years they no longer issued documents, but placed several hundred white-clad watchers in the two markets and busy wards and lanes to inspect what people sold;
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the eunuchs stopped using written orders and instead posted hundreds of agents in the markets and busy streets to inspect goods for sale;

sentences.zh: 但稱宮市，則斂手付與，真偽不復可辨，無敢問所從來及論價之高下者。

translations.literal: if they merely said "palace market," people folded their hands and handed goods over; genuine and false could no longer be distinguished, and none dared ask whence things came or debate whether prices were high or low.
translations.idiomatic: at the word "palace market" merchants handed over their goods without question; none dared ask provenance or haggle over price.

sentences.zh: 率用直百錢物買人直數千物，仍索進奉門戶及腳價銀。

translations.literal: They routinely used goods worth a hundred cash to buy goods worth several thousand, and still demanded tribute gate fees and porterage silver.
translations.idiomatic: They routinely paid a pittance for goods worth far more, and still demanded gate fees and porterage silver on top.

sentences.zh: 人將物詣市，至有空手而歸者，名為宮市，其實奪之。

translations.literal: People brought goods to market and some returned empty-handed; it was called palace market, but in truth it was seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants sometimes went to market and returned empty-handed; it was called the palace market, but it was outright seizure.

sentences.zh: 嘗有農夫以驢馱柴，宦者市之，與絹數尺，又就索門戶，仍邀驢送柴至內。

translations.literal: Once a farmer carried firewood on a donkey; a eunuch bought it, gave several feet of silk, then demanded gate fees and still insisted the donkey deliver the firewood inside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once a farmer brought firewood on a donkey; a eunuch "bought" it for a few feet of silk, demanded gate fees, and insisted the donkey carry the wood into the palace.

sentences.zh: 農夫啼泣，以所得絹與之，不肯受，曰：「須得爾驢。」

translations.literal: The farmer wept and offered back the silk he had received, but the eunuch would not accept it and said, "I must have your donkey."
translations.idiomatic: The farmer wept and tried to return the silk, but the eunuch refused and said, "I want your donkey.

sentences.zh: 農夫曰：「我有父母妻子，待此而後食；

translations.literal: The farmer said, "I have parents, wife, and children who depend on this to eat;
translations.idiomatic: The farmer said, "My parents, wife, and children depend on this donkey to live;

sentences.zh: 今與汝柴，而不取直而歸，汝尚不肯，我有死而已。」

translations.literal: now I have given you the firewood and return without payment, yet you still refuse—I have only death left."
translations.idiomatic: I have given you the wood and taken no payment, yet you still refuse me—then I have nothing left but to die.

sentences.zh: 遂毆宦者。

translations.literal: He then beat the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck the eunuch.

sentences.zh: 街使擒之以聞，乃黜宦者，賜農夫絹十匹。

translations.literal: The street commissioner seized him and reported; the eunuch was dismissed and the farmer was granted ten bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Street guards seized him and reported the affair; the eunuch was punished and the farmer was given ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 然宮市不為之改，諫宮御史表疏論列，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Yet the palace market was not changed on that account; remonstrance officials and censors submitted memorials discussing it, but all were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: The palace market continued unchanged; remonstrance officials and censors memorialized against it, but the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 吳湊以戚裏為京兆尹，深言其弊。

translations.literal: Wu Cou, as an imperial in-law serving as Jingzhao magistrate, spoke deeply of its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cou, an imperial in-law serving as Jingzhao magistrate, spoke out forcefully against the abuse.

sentences.zh: 建封入覲，具奏之，德宗頗深嘉納；

translations.literal: When Jianfeng entered court, he submitted a full memorial on it, and Dezong greatly approved and accepted it;
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng came to court he memorialized on the practice in full, and Emperor Dezong was much impressed;

sentences.zh: 而戶部侍郎、判度支蘇弁希宦者之旨，因入奏事，上問之，弁對曰：「京師遊手墮業者數千萬家，無土著生業，仰宮市取給。」

translations.literal: but Revenue vice minister and revenue commissioner Su Bian curried the eunuchs' intent; when he entered to report on affairs the emperor questioned him, and Bian replied, "In the capital several tens of thousands of idle households have no settled livelihood and rely on the palace market for support."
translations.idiomatic: but Revenue vice minister Su Bian, who favored the eunuchs, told the emperor when asked that tens of thousands of idle households in the capital had no livelihood and depended on the palace market.

sentences.zh: 上信之，凡言宮市者皆不聽用。

translations.literal: The emperor believed this, and all who spoke of the palace market were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him, and every proposal to reform the palace market was rejected.

sentences.zh: 詔書矜免百姓諸色逋賦，上問建封，對曰：「凡逋賦殘欠，皆是累積年月，無可征收，雖蒙陛下憂恤，百姓亦無所裨益。」

translations.literal: An edict compassionately remitted the people's various overdue levies; the emperor asked Jianfeng, who replied, "All overdue arrears have accumulated over years and cannot be collected; though Your Majesty shows concern and relief, the common people gain no real benefit."
translations.idiomatic: When an edict compassionately remitted overdue taxes, the emperor asked Jianfeng, who replied, "These arrears have piled up over years and cannot be collected; though Your Majesty means well, the people will gain nothing from it.

sentences.zh: 時河東節度使李說、華州刺史盧微，皆中風疾，口不能言，足不能行，但信任左右胥吏決遣之。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong military governor Li Shuo and Huazhou prefect Lu Wei both suffered wind-stroke illness, could not speak or walk, and only trusted the clerks at their sides to decide and dispatch affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hedong governor Li Shuo and Huazhou prefect Lu Wei were both paralyzed by stroke and could only let their clerks run their commands.

sentences.zh: 建封皆悉聞奏，上深嘉納。

translations.literal: Jianfeng heard of all these and memorialized; the emperor deeply approved and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng reported all of this as well, and the emperor again approved his counsel.

sentences.zh: 又金吾大將軍李翰好伺察城中細事，加諸聞奏，冀求恩寵，人畏而惡之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Golden Guard great general Li Han loved to spy on minor matters in the city and report them upward, hoping to win favor; people feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard general Li Han also loved to spy on petty affairs in the capital and report them upward for favor; people feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 建封亦奏之，乃下詔曰：「比來朝官或諸處過從，金吾皆有上聞。
