translations.literal: Jianfeng also memorialized on this, and an edict was issued: "Recently when court officials visited one another here and there, the Golden Guard reported everything upward.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng memorialized on this too, and an edict followed: "Lately the Golden Guard has reported every social visit among court officials.

sentences.zh: 其間如素是親故，或曾同僚友，伏臘歲序，時有還往，亦是常禮，人情所通。

translations.literal: Among them, those who were old friends or former colleagues exchanging visits at seasonal festivals are also ordinary ritual and what human feeling permits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet visits among old friends and former colleagues at seasonal festivals are ordinary courtesy and natural human feeling.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，金吾不須聞。」

translations.literal: From now on the Golden Guard need not report such matters."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Golden Guard need not report such matters."

sentences.zh: 十四年春上巳，賜宰臣百僚宴於曲江亭，特令建封與宰相同座而食。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year, on the Shangsi festival, the chief ministers and hundred officials were granted a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion; Jianfeng was specially ordered to sit and eat at the same table as the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourteenth year, on the Shangsi festival, the emperor gave the chief ministers and officials a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion and specially seated Jianfeng at the chief ministers' table.

sentences.zh: 貞元已後，籓帥入朝及還鎮，如馬燧、渾瑊、劉玄佐、李抱真、曲環之崇秩鴻勛，未有獲禦制詩以送者，建封將還鎮，特賜詩曰：「牧守寄所重，才賢生為時。

translations.literal: After Zhenyuan, when frontier commanders entered court or returned to their commands—such as Ma Sui, Hun Jian, Liu Xuanzuo, Li Baozhen, and Qu Huan with their lofty ranks and great merit—none had received an imperially composed farewell poem; as Jianfeng was about to return to his command, a poem was specially granted, saying, "Prefects and guards are entrusted with what is weighty; talent and worth are born for the age.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenyuan, eminent frontier commanders such as Ma Sui, Hun Jian, Liu Xuanzuo, Li Baozhen, and Qu Huan had never been sent back to their posts with an imperial farewell poem; as Jianfeng prepared to return, the emperor specially granted one that began, "The realm entrusts its prefects with weighty charge; talent is born for its age.

sentences.zh: 宣風自淮甸，授鉞膺籓維。

translations.literal: You spread influence from the Huai region and received the axe to bear the frontier screen.
translations.idiomatic: You spread good governance from the Huai region and took the command baton to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 入覲展遐戀，臨軒慰來思。

translations.literal: Entering court you displayed long-distant devotion; at the throne we comforted your returning thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: At court you showed your distant loyalty; from the throne we comforted your homesick heart.

sentences.zh: 忠誠在方寸，感激陳清詞。

translations.literal: Loyalty and sincerity dwell in your breast; moved, you offered clear words.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty filled your breast, and in gratitude you spoke with clarity.

sentences.zh: 報國爾所尚，恤人予是資。

translations.literal: Serving the state is what you esteem; caring for the people is what I rely on you for.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the state is your aim; caring for the people is how you aid me.

sentences.zh: 歡宴不盡懷，車馬當還期。

translations.literal: Feasting cannot exhaust our feelings; horses and chariots must keep to the time of return.
translations.idiomatic: Our feast cannot hold back parting; your horses must keep to their homeward date.

sentences.zh: 谷雨將應候，行春猶未遲。

translations.literal: Grain Rain will soon answer the season; the spring journey is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: Grain Rain is near; it is not yet too late to set out for spring.

sentences.zh: 勿以千里遙，而雲無已知。」

translations.literal: Do not, because a thousand li are distant, say that none knows you."
translations.idiomatic: Do not say, because you are a thousand li away, that you are unknown to us.

sentences.zh: 又令高品中使賫常所執鞭以賜之，曰：「以卿忠貞節義，歲寒不移，此鞭朕久執用，故以賜卿，表卿忠節也。」

translations.literal: He also ordered a high-ranking palace envoy to bring the whip he habitually carried and grant it, saying, "Because you are loyal, upright, and constant in integrity, unchanging in the year's cold, this whip I have long held and used—I therefore grant it to you to mark your loyal integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a senior palace envoy with the whip he habitually carried, saying, "Your loyalty and integrity never waver in hard times; I have long used this whip, and I give it to you as a mark of your constancy."

sentences.zh: 建封又獻詩一篇，以自警勵。

translations.literal: Jianfeng also presented one poem as self-admonition and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng presented a poem in return as his own pledge of resolve.

sentences.zh: 建封在彭城十年，軍州稱理。

translations.literal: Jianfeng was at Pengcheng for ten years, and army and prefecture were said to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng governed at Pengcheng for ten years, and both army and prefecture were said to be well ordered.

sentences.zh: 復又禮賢下士，無賢不肖，遊其門者，皆禮遇之，天下名士向風延頸，其往如歸。

translations.literal: Moreover he honored the worthy and humbled himself before scholars; whether worthy or not, all who came to his gate were treated with courtesy; famous scholars throughout the realm turned toward his wind and stretched their necks, going to him as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He honored scholars and welcomed all who came to his gate, worthy or not; men of letters across the empire turned toward him and came as if to a home of their own.

sentences.zh: 貞元時，文人如許孟容、韓愈諸公，皆為之從事。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, literary men such as Xu Mengrong, Han Yu, and others all served on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era, writers such as Xu Mengrong and Han Yu served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遇疾，連上表請速除代，方用韋夏卿為徐泗行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he fell ill and repeatedly submitted memorials asking for a speedy replacement; only then was Wei Xiaqing appointed Xu-Si campaign staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he fell ill and repeatedly asked for a successor; Wei Xiaqing was then named Xu–Si campaign staff officer.

sentences.zh: 未至而建封卒，時年六十六，冊贈司徒。

translations.literal: Before he arrived Jianfeng died at the age of sixty-six; he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand mentor by patent.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaqing arrived, Jianfeng died at sixty-six; the court posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 子愔。

translations.literal: His son Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yin.

sentences.zh: 愔以廕授虢州參軍。

translations.literal: Yin received by privilege the post of Guo Prefecture staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yin entered office by privilege as staff officer in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，建封卒，判官鄭通誠權知留後事。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng first died, judge Zheng Tongcheng acted as temporary rear administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianfeng died, his judge Zheng Tongcheng acted as temporary rear administrator.

sentences.zh: 通誠懼軍士謀亂，適遇浙西兵遷鎮，通誠欲引入州城為援。

translations.literal: Tongcheng feared the soldiers would plot disorder; it happened that Zhexi troops were transferring their command, and Tongcheng wished to bring them into the prefectural city as support.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng feared mutiny and, when Zhexi troops happened to be passing through on transfer, tried to bring them into the city as support.

sentences.zh: 事泄，三軍怒，五六千人斫甲仗庫取戈甲，執帶環繞衙城，請愔為留後。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; the three armies were enraged; five or six thousand men hacked open the armory and took spears and armor, seized their belts, and surrounded the headquarters, asking that Yin be made rear administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked, five or six thousand troops stormed the armory, armed themselves, surrounded headquarters, and demanded Yin as acting commander.

sentences.zh: 乃殺通誠、楊德宗、大將段伯熊、吉遂、曲澄、張秀等。

translations.literal: They then killed Tongcheng, Yang Dezong, great generals Duan Boxiong, Ji Sui, Qu Cheng, Zhang Xiu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Tongcheng, Yang Dezong, and the senior officers Duan Boxiong, Ji Sui, Qu Cheng, Zhang Xiu, and others.

sentences.zh: 軍眾請於朝廷，乞授愔旄節。

translations.literal: The army masses petitioned the court, begging that Yin be granted the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: The troops petitioned the court to grant Yin the command baton.

sentences.zh: 初不之許，乃割濠、泗二州隸淮南，加杜佑同平章事以討徐州。

translations.literal: At first this was not granted; Hao and Si prefectures were cut away and placed under Huainan, and Du You was made associate director of the Imperial Secretariat to attack Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court refused, detached Hao and Si to Huainan control, and named Du You associate director of the Imperial Secretariat to campaign against Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而泗州刺史張伾以兵攻埇橋，與徐軍接戰，伾大敗而還。

translations.literal: Thereafter Si Prefecture prefect Zhang Pi attacked Yongqiao with troops, engaged the Xu army, and Pi was greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Si prefect Zhang Pi then attacked Yongqiao, was beaten by the Xu troops, and retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，乃授愔起復右驍衛將軍同正，兼徐州刺史、御史中丞，充本州團練使，知徐州留後。

translations.literal: The court, having no alternative, appointed Yin, recalled from mourning, right Brave Guards general with regular salary, concurrently Xuzhou prefect and vice censor-in-chief, regimental commissioner of his prefecture, and acting Xu rear administrator.
translations.idiomatic: With no other choice, the court recalled Yin from mourning as right Brave Guards general, concurrently Xuzhou prefect, vice censor-in-chief, regimental commissioner, and acting rear administrator.

sentences.zh: 仍以泗州刺史張伾為泗州留後，濠州刺史杜兼為濠州留後。

translations.literal: Zhang Pi remained Si Prefecture rear administrator, and Du Jian remained Hao Prefecture rear administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi remained acting Si prefect, and Du Jian acting Hao prefect.

sentences.zh: 正授武寧軍節度、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed Wuning Army military governor and acting minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed military governor of the Wuning Army and acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，被疾，上表請代，征為兵部尚書，以東都留守王紹為武寧軍節度代愔，復隸濠、泗二州於徐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he fell ill, submitted a memorial requesting replacement, was summoned as minister of war, and Eastern Capital regent Wang Shao was made Wuning military governor to replace Yin; Hao and Si were again subordinated to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 1 he fell ill and asked to be replaced; the court summoned him as minister of war, sent Wang Shao as Wuning military governor in his place, and restored Hao and Si to Xu jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 徐軍喜復得二州，不敢為亂，而愔遂赴京師，未出界卒。

translations.literal: The Xu army rejoiced at regaining the two prefectures and did not dare make trouble; Yin then set out for the capital but died before leaving the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu troops, glad to regain the two prefectures, did not rebel; Yin set out for the capital but died before crossing the border.

sentences.zh: 愔在徐州七年，百姓稱理，詔贈右僕射。

translations.literal: Yin was at Xuzhou for seven years; the common people said he governed well, and an edict posthumously made him right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yin governed Xuzhou for seven years to general approval; the court posthumously named him right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，入拜侍御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he entered court and was appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 6 he entered court as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 有人誣告故尚父子儀嬖人張氏宅中有寶玉者，張氏兄弟又與尚父家子孫相告訴，詔促按其獄。

translations.literal: Someone falsely accused the late Grand Mentor Guo Ziyi's favorite Zhang's household of holding precious jade; Zhang's brothers also sued one another with the Grand Mentor's descendants, and an edict urgently ordered investigation of the case.
translations.idiomatic: Someone falsely accused the household of Guo Ziyi's late favorite Zhang of hoarding jade; Zhang's brothers also sued the Guo family heirs, and the court ordered a hurried investigation.

sentences.zh: 群奏曰：「張氏以子儀在時分財，子弟不合爭奪。

translations.literal: Qun memorialized, saying, "The Zhang family divided property while Ziyi was alive; the sons and younger kin ought not to fight over it.
translations.idiomatic: Qun memorialized, "The Zhang family divided the estate while Ziyi was alive; his descendants ought not to fight over it now.

sentences.zh: 然張氏宅與子儀親仁宅，皆子儀家事。

translations.literal: Yet Zhang's residence and Ziyi's Qinren residence are both Ziyi's household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zhang's house and Ziyi's Qinren mansion are both family matters of the Guo house.

sentences.zh: 子儀有大勛，伏望陛下特赦而勿問，俾私自引退。」

translations.literal: Ziyi rendered great merit; I humbly hope Your Majesty will specially pardon and not inquire, allowing them to withdraw of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi rendered great service to the state; I beg Your Majesty to pardon the matter and let the family settle it privately.

sentences.zh: 德宗從其言，時人嘉其識大體。

translations.literal: Dezong followed his words, and people of the time praised his grasp of larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong accepted his advice, and contemporaries praised his sense of larger principle.

sentences.zh: 累轉左司、職方、兵部三員外郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred among the three posts of left secretariat, bureau of appointments, and ministry of war extra bureau directors.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through extra bureau director posts in the left secretariat, appointments bureau, and ministry of war.

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使吳少誠擅開決司、洧等水漕輓溉田，遣中使止之，少誠不奉詔。

translations.literal: Huai West military governor Wu Shaocheng on his own authority opened the Juesi, Wei, and other waterways to transport grain and irrigate fields; a palace envoy was sent to stop him, but Shaocheng did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Huai West governor Wu Shaocheng opened the Juesi and Wei waterways on his own authority to irrigate fields; when a palace envoy ordered him to stop, he refused.

sentences.zh: 令群使蔡州詰之，少誠曰：「開大渠，大利於人。」

translations.literal: Qun was ordered as envoy to Cai Prefecture to question him; Shaocheng said, "Opening the great canal greatly benefits the people."
translations.idiomatic: Qun was sent to Cai Prefecture to question him; Shaocheng replied, "Opening the great canal greatly benefits the people.

sentences.zh: 群曰：「為臣之道，不合自專，雖便於人，須俟君命。

translations.literal: Qun said, "The way of serving as minister does not permit acting on one's own; though it benefits people, one must await the ruler's command.
translations.idiomatic: Qun replied, "A subject must not act on his own authority; even if the work benefits the people, he must await the throne's command.

sentences.zh: 且人臣須以恭恪為事，若事君不盡恭恪，即責下吏恭恪，固亦難矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover a subject must take reverent care as his task; if in serving the ruler he is not fully reverent and careful, then to demand reverent care from subordinate officials is likewise difficult."
translations.idiomatic: And if a minister is not reverent toward his ruler, how can he demand reverence from his subordinates?"

sentences.zh: 凡數百千言，諭以君臣之分，忠順之義，少誠乃從命，即停工役。

translations.literal: In all several thousand words he instructed him in the distinction of ruler and minister and the principle of loyalty and obedience; Shaocheng then followed the command and immediately halted the labor.
translations.idiomatic: In several thousand words he expounded the duties of ruler and subject and the meaning of loyalty; Shaocheng obeyed and halted the project at once.

sentences.zh: 群博涉，有口辨，好談論，與少誠言古今成敗之事，無不聳聽。

translations.literal: Qun was broadly learned, had eloquence, loved discussion; when he spoke with Shaocheng of success and failure in past and present, none failed to listen with rapt attention.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was learned and eloquent and loved debate; when he discussed past rises and falls with Shaocheng, every listener was riveted.

sentences.zh: 又與唱和賦詩，自言以反側，常蒙隔在恩外，群於筵中醉而歌曰：「祥瑞不在鳳凰、麒麟，太平須得邊將、忠臣。

translations.literal: They also exchanged verses in song; Shaocheng said that because he had been a rebel he was often kept outside imperial favor; Qun, drunk at the feast, sang, "Auspicious omens lie not in phoenix or qilin; great peace requires frontier generals and loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They also exchanged poems; Shaocheng said that as a former rebel he had long stood outside imperial favor; Qun, drunk at the banquet, sang, "Peace does not depend on phoenixes or qilin; it depends on frontier generals and loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 衛、霍真誠奉主，貔虎十萬一身。

translations.literal: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing truly served their lord; a hundred thousand tiger warriors were one body.
translations.idiomatic: Like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing they serve the throne in truth; a hundred thousand warriors are one man.

sentences.zh: 江、河潛註息浪，蠻貊款塞無塵。

translations.literal: The Yangzi and Yellow rivers secretly pour forth and still their waves; barbarians sincerely close the passes and no dust rises.
translations.idiomatic: The rivers run calm, the frontier tribes keep the passes, and no dust of war rises.

sentences.zh: 但得百僚師長肝膽，不用三軍羅綺金銀。」

translations.literal: Only obtain the liver and gall of the hundred officials as teachers and elders—there is no need for the three armies' silks, brocades, gold, and silver."
translations.idiomatic: Give us ministers with open hearts, and we need not the army's silks and gold.

sentences.zh: 少誠大感悅。

translations.literal: Shaocheng was greatly moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 群以奉使稱旨，俄遷檢校秘書監，兼御史中丞、義成軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Because Qun's mission accorded with the imperial intent, he was soon promoted to acting director of the Secretariat, concurrently vice censor-in-chief and Yicheng Army campaign staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mission pleased the throne, Qun was soon made acting director of the Secretariat, concurrently vice censor-in-chief and Yicheng Army campaign staff officer.

sentences.zh: 貞元十六年四月，節度姚南仲歸朝，拜群義成軍節度、鄭滑觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan, when military governor Yao Nanzhong returned to court, Qun was appointed Yicheng military governor and Zheng-Hua observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhenyuan 16, when Yao Nanzhong returned to court, Qun was appointed military governor of Yicheng and observation commissioner of Zheng–Hua.

sentences.zh: 先寓居鄭州，典質良田數頃；

translations.literal: He had earlier lived in Zheng Prefecture and pawned several qing of good farmland;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while living in Zheng Prefecture, he had pawned several qing of good farmland;

sentences.zh: 及為節度使至鎮，各與本地契書，分付所管令長，令召還本主，時論稱美。

translations.literal: when he became military governor and reached his command, he matched each with local contracts, handed them to the magistrates under his authority, and ordered the original owners summoned back; opinion of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: when he took command as military governor, he matched each parcel to its local contract, ordered the magistrates to return the land to the original owners, and won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 尋遇疾，其年十月卒，時年五十九，廢朝一日，贈工部尚書，赗賻布帛、米粟有差。

translations.literal: Soon he fell ill; in the tenth month of that year he died at the age of fifty-nine; court was suspended one day; he was posthumously made minister of works; funeral gifts of cloth, silk, grain, and millet were granted in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died that tenth month at fifty-nine; the court suspended audiences for a day, posthumously named him minister of works, and granted graded funeral gifts of cloth and grain.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：韋南康、張徐州，慷慨下位之中，橫身喪亂之際，力扶衰運，氣激壯圖，義風凜凜，聳動群醜，舂盜之喉，折賊之角，可謂忠矣！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wei of Nankang and Zhang of Xuzhou, amid generous spirit in low station and throwing themselves across the age of chaos, strove to uphold the declining fortune, roused their spirit to great designs, with righteous wind stern and cold, startling the crowd of villains, pounding the robbers' throats and breaking the rebels' horns—truly loyal!
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Wei of Nankang and Zhang of Xuzhou rose from humble stations in an age of chaos, upheld a failing dynasty, and with stern righteousness stunned the villains, crushed the rebels' power, and broke their horns—men truly loyal!

sentences.zh: 而韋公季年，惑賊辟之奸說，欲兼巴、益，則誌未可量。

translations.literal: Yet in his later years Lord Wei was deluded by the traitor Pi's wicked persuasion and wished to annex Ba and Yi—then his ambition cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his later years Wei was swayed by Liu Pi's treacherous counsel and aimed at Ba and Yi as well—ambition beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 徐州請覲，頗有規諫之言，所謂以道匡君，能以功名始終者。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou man's request to attend court carried much admonitory counsel—what is called using the Way to correct the ruler, able to begin and end in merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's visit to court brought forceful remonstrance—using the Way to correct the ruler and seeing merit through to the end.

sentences.zh: 盧載初喻少誠，還地券，君子哉！

translations.literal: Lu Zai at first instructed Shaocheng and returned land contracts—a gentleman indeed!
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zai first persuaded Shaocheng and returned land contracts—a gentleman indeed!

sentences.zh: 三子之賢，不可多得。

translations.literal: Such worth among these three men cannot easily be found again.
translations.idiomatic: Such worth in these three men is not easily found again.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：南康英壯，力匡交喪。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Nankang, heroic and stalwart, strove to right the age of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Nankang, heroic and strong, righted the age of ruin.

sentences.zh: 張侯義烈，誌平亂象。

translations.literal: Marquis Zhang, righteous and fierce, set his will on pacifying the signs of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Zhang, righteous and fierce, resolved to end the omens of chaos.

sentences.zh: 見危能振，蹈利無謗。

translations.literal: Seeing peril he could rouse himself; treading profit he incurred no slander.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied in peril and took profit without reproach.

sentences.zh: 韋德不周，張心可亮。

translations.literal: Wei's virtue was not complete; Zhang's heart may be shown bright.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's virtue fell short; Zhang's heart shines clear.
